name: Policy review currency
definition: Share of information-security policies and standards that have been reviewed and approved within their review period (usually 12 months).
formula: policies reviewed within period / total policies in the policy register x 100
data_source: Policy register (GRC tool or document management)
pitfalls: Rubber-stamp reviews that change a date and nothing else. | Counting drafts as policies inflates the denominator.

name: Risk treatment actions overdue
definition: Number of risk-treatment actions in the risk register whose target date has passed without closure.
formula: count of open actions with target date < today
data_source: Risk register
target_example: 0 overdue on High or Critical risks; <= 5 in total
pitfalls: Moving target dates instead of closing actions hides the backlog; also track date changes. | Weight by risk rating, or one overdue Critical looks like one overdue Low.

name: Control coverage against framework
definition: Share of applicable framework controls (for example ISO/IEC 27001 Annex A or CIS v8 IG2) assessed as implemented and evidenced.
formula: controls implemented with evidence / applicable controls x 100
data_source: Control assessment or Statement of Applicability
pitfalls: Self-assessed 'implemented' without evidence is opinion, not coverage. | A single percentage hides which domains are weak; show the breakdown.

name: Audit findings open past due
definition: Internal and external audit findings (security scope) that remain open after their agreed remediation date.
formula: count of open findings with due date < today
data_source: Audit tracker
target_example: 0 past due; all findings have an owner and a date
pitfalls: Closing a finding on a promise rather than on evidence. | Repeat findings should count more than new ones.

name: Asset inventory completeness
definition: Share of discovered devices and applications that have a named owner and a classification in the inventory.
formula: inventory items with owner and classification / items discovered by network, EDR and SaaS discovery x 100
data_source: CMDB or asset inventory reconciled against EDR, network discovery and SaaS discovery
pitfalls: Only measuring against what the inventory already knows; the denominator must come from discovery. | Owners that have left the company still count as owners unless you reconcile with HR.

name: MFA coverage (all users)
definition: Share of enabled user accounts that must complete multi-factor authentication to sign in to corporate applications.
formula: enabled users with MFA enforced / enabled users x 100
data_source: Identity provider sign-in and authentication-method reports
pitfalls: Registered is not enforced; count accounts where a policy requires MFA. | Legacy authentication protocols can bypass MFA; pair with a legacy-auth sign-in count. | Excluded accounts (break-glass, service) must be listed, not hidden.

name: Phishing-resistant MFA for privileged roles
definition: Share of accounts holding administrative roles that are required to use a phishing-resistant method (FIDO2 key, passkey or certificate).
formula: admin accounts with phishing-resistant method enforced / admin accounts x 100
data_source: Identity provider role assignments and authentication-strength policies
pitfalls: Eligible (just-in-time) role holders must be included, not only permanently active ones. | A method that is available but not required by policy does not count.

name: Privileged accounts per administrator
definition: Number of accounts holding high-privilege roles (global, domain, cloud-owner equivalents) relative to the number of people who need them.
formula: accounts with high-privilege roles / people with an approved admin role
data_source: Identity provider, directory, cloud IAM
pitfalls: Service principals and automation identities with admin rights are often forgotten. | Ratio alone hides a large absolute number; report both.

name: Dormant accounts
definition: Enabled accounts (user and service) with no successful sign-in in the last 90 days.
formula: enabled accounts with last sign-in > 90 days ago (count and % of enabled accounts)
data_source: Identity provider sign-in logs, directory last-logon attributes
target_example: < 1 % of enabled accounts; 0 with privileged roles
pitfalls: Shared mailboxes and room resources appear dormant by design; exclude them explicitly. | Disabling without deleting leaves tokens and group memberships; track the full lifecycle.

name: Leaver de-provisioning time
definition: Time between the HR-recorded leaving date (or termination notice) and the disabling of all the leaver's accounts.
formula: median hours from leave date to last account disabled, over leavers in the period
data_source: HR system export joined with identity provider audit log
pitfalls: Only measuring the directory account; SaaS applications with local accounts are the usual leak. | Median hides the one leaver still enabled after 60 days; also report the maximum.

name: Access review completion
definition: Share of scheduled periodic access reviews (privileged roles, sensitive groups, key applications) completed by their due date, with decisions recorded.
formula: reviews completed on time / reviews scheduled x 100
data_source: Identity governance tool or review tracker
pitfalls: A review that approves 100 % of access in seconds is not a review; track the revocation rate too. | Auto-approval on timeout counts as complete in some tools; exclude it.

name: Service accounts with non-expiring credentials
definition: Service accounts, API keys and application secrets whose credential has no expiry or is older than the policy maximum.
formula: count of credentials with no expiry or age > policy maximum
data_source: Directory, cloud IAM, secrets vault, application registrations
target_example: 0 older than 12 months; all in a vault
pitfalls: Rotating the password but keeping the old one valid in a second application. | Secrets embedded in code are invisible to this metric; pair with a secrets-scanning count.

name: Critical vulnerabilities remediated within SLA
definition: Share of critical-severity vulnerabilities (by your internal rating, which should include exploit availability) that were fixed or compensated within the policy SLA.
formula: critical vulnerabilities closed within SLA / critical vulnerabilities due in the period x 100
data_source: Vulnerability scanner, ticketing system
pitfalls: Re-rating vulnerabilities to High to meet the Critical SLA; audit severity changes. | Risk accepted must be a visible category with an expiry, not a way to close.

name: Mean time to remediate critical vulnerabilities
definition: Average number of days between first detection and verified remediation of critical vulnerabilities closed in the period.
formula: sum of (closed date - first seen date) / critical vulnerabilities closed in the period
data_source: Vulnerability scanner
pitfalls: Only closed items count, so a growing backlog of very old items makes the mean look better. | Use the scanner's first-seen date, not the ticket creation date.

name: Known-exploited vulnerabilities on internet-facing assets
definition: Number of vulnerabilities listed in a known-exploited catalogue that are currently open on assets reachable from the internet.
formula: count of open findings on external assets matching the known-exploited list
data_source: External attack-surface scanning, vulnerability scanner, known-exploited vulnerability catalogue
pitfalls: Depends entirely on the external asset list being complete; pair with VUL-06. | A vulnerability behind a WAF rule is mitigated, not fixed; show both states.

name: Vulnerability scan coverage
definition: Share of in-scope assets (servers, workstations, containers, cloud resources) that were successfully scanned, with credentials where applicable, in the last cycle.
formula: assets scanned with authenticated or agent-based scan in period / in-scope assets x 100
data_source: Vulnerability scanner reconciled against the asset inventory
pitfalls: Unauthenticated scans find a fraction of the issues; count them separately. | The denominator must come from the inventory (GOV-05), not from the scanner itself.

name: Median age of open high and critical vulnerabilities
definition: Median number of days since first detection across all currently open high and critical vulnerabilities.
formula: median(today - first seen date) over open high and critical findings
data_source: Vulnerability scanner
pitfalls: Mass-closing stale findings without a fix resets the clock; require verification scans. | Complements VUL-02: VUL-02 looks at what was fixed, VUL-05 at what is still open.

name: Unexpected internet-exposed services
definition: Services reachable from the internet that are not on the approved exposure list (unknown hosts, open management ports, forgotten test systems).
formula: count of external services discovered minus services on the approved list
data_source: External attack-surface management, cloud configuration export, firewall rules
target_example: 0 unapproved; every finding triaged within 48 hours
pitfalls: Adding every discovery to the approved list to reach zero defeats the purpose; approvals need an owner. | Scan from outside your own network, otherwise you measure your firewall's view of itself.

name: EDR coverage
definition: Share of in-scope endpoints and servers running a healthy endpoint detection and response agent that reported in the last 7 days.
formula: devices with healthy EDR agent reporting in 7 days / devices in inventory x 100
data_source: EDR console reconciled with asset inventory and directory
pitfalls: An installed but non-reporting agent is not coverage; use the last-seen date. | Using the EDR console as its own denominator always gives 100 %.

name: Patch compliance (operating system)
definition: Share of managed devices that have installed the current month's operating-system security updates within 30 days of release.
formula: devices fully patched within 30 days / managed devices x 100
data_source: Patch management or device management console
pitfalls: Devices that have not checked in are often excluded automatically, hiding the worst cases. | Applications and firmware matter too; this metric covers the OS only.

name: Unsupported operating systems
definition: Devices running an operating system version that no longer receives security updates from the vendor.
formula: count of devices with end-of-support OS (and % of managed devices)
data_source: Device management, EDR or vulnerability scanner OS inventory
target_example: 0 on user devices; servers isolated with a documented exception
pitfalls: Embedded and operational-technology devices are frequently out of scope by omission. | Extended-support contracts delay the problem; track the end date.

name: Disk encryption coverage
definition: Share of laptops and mobile devices with full-disk encryption enforced and recovery keys escrowed.
formula: devices with encryption enforced and key escrowed / portable devices x 100
data_source: Device management console
pitfalls: Encrypted without an escrowed key becomes a data-loss incident at the first forgotten PIN. | Personal devices with corporate data under a bring-your-own policy are usually unmeasured.

name: Hardening baseline compliance
definition: Share of managed devices compliant with the organisation's security baseline (configuration profile, attack-surface-reduction rules, local-admin restrictions).
formula: devices reporting compliant to all baseline policies / managed devices x 100
data_source: Device management compliance reports
pitfalls: Loosening the baseline to raise compliance; version the baseline and report changes. | Rules in audit mode are not enforcement; report block mode separately.

name: Mean time to detect
definition: Average time between the first malicious activity (as established in the investigation) and the first alert or report that started the response.
formula: sum of (first alert time - attacker first activity time) / incidents closed in the period
data_source: Incident records with reconstructed timelines
pitfalls: Needs a reconstructed timeline per incident; without one the number is a guess. | Small incident counts make the mean swing wildly; show the number of incidents behind it.

name: Mean time to contain
definition: Average time between an incident being declared and the attacker's access being removed or the affected asset isolated.
formula: sum of (containment time - declaration time) / incidents in the period
data_source: Incident records, ticketing timestamps
target_example: <= 4 hours for High and Critical incidents
pitfalls: Containment is not resolution; a separate metric for full recovery avoids mixing the two. | Mean is dominated by the one weekend incident; report median and maximum alongside.

name: Alert triage within SLA
definition: Share of security alerts that received a first analyst action within the time allowed for their severity.
formula: alerts triaged within SLA / alerts raised in the period x 100
data_source: SIEM or SOAR case management
pitfalls: Auto-closing alerts counts as triage in some tools; exclude automated closures. | Tuning noisy rules improves this metric honestly; suppressing them silently does not.

name: Log source coverage of critical assets
definition: Share of assets classified as critical whose security logs are received by the SIEM and have been seen in the last 24 hours.
formula: critical assets with logs received in 24 hours / critical assets x 100
data_source: SIEM data-source health, asset inventory
pitfalls: Receiving logs is not the same as parsing them; a broken parser gives a green light and no detections. | Identity and SaaS logs are as critical as server logs and more often missing.

name: False-positive rate
definition: Share of security alerts closed as benign or false positive after analyst review.
formula: alerts closed as false positive / alerts reviewed x 100
data_source: SIEM or SOAR case outcomes
pitfalls: Driving the rate to zero usually means detections were removed, not improved. | Classify 'benign true positive' (expected activity that matched) separately from 'false positive'.

name: Security incidents by severity
definition: Number of confirmed security incidents declared in the period, broken down by severity level.
formula: count of incidents per severity in the period
data_source: Incident register
target_example: 0 Critical; trend of High and Medium flat or down
pitfalls: A rising count after better detection is good news; present it with DR-04 and DR-07. | Severity definitions must be written down or the mix shifts with whoever is on shift.

name: Detection coverage of priority techniques
definition: Share of the organisation's priority list of adversary techniques (for example 30 MITRE ATT&CK techniques chosen from threat modelling) that have at least one tested detection.
formula: priority techniques with a validated detection / priority techniques x 100
data_source: Detection engineering backlog, ATT&CK mapping of rules, purple-team results
pitfalls: A rule that exists but has never fired or been tested is not coverage; require a test record. | Coverage of the whole ATT&CK matrix is a vanity number; use a prioritised list.

name: Incident exercises completed
definition: Number of tabletop or technical incident-response exercises run in the period, with actions tracked to closure.
formula: exercises completed in period (and share of resulting actions closed)
data_source: Exercise reports, action tracker
target_example: >= 1 per quarter, including one with executives per year
pitfalls: Exercises with no findings were too easy or not written up honestly. | Count only exercises whose actions are tracked; otherwise it is theatre.

name: Phishing simulation click rate
definition: Share of recipients who clicked the link or opened the attachment in a simulated phishing campaign.
formula: recipients who clicked / emails delivered x 100
data_source: Phishing simulation platform
pitfalls: Easier templates lower the rate; record the difficulty level with every campaign. | Punitive follow-up drives under-reporting of real phishing; use AWR-02 as the primary metric.

name: Phishing report rate
definition: Share of recipients of a simulated phishing email who reported it through the official reporting button or process.
formula: recipients who reported / emails delivered x 100
data_source: Phishing simulation platform, mail reporting add-in
pitfalls: Reports after clicking are still valuable; count them but show them separately. | If the reporting button is hard to find, the metric measures the button, not the people.

name: Security training completion
definition: Share of staff and contractors who completed the mandatory security awareness training within the required window (at hire and annually).
formula: people completed within window / people required x 100
data_source: Learning management system joined with HR headcount
pitfalls: Completion says nothing about understanding; pair with a short assessment pass rate. | Contractors and long-term leave are usually excluded by accident; define the denominator.

name: Repeat clickers
definition: People who clicked in two or more simulated phishing campaigns in the last 12 months.
formula: count of people with >= 2 clicks in 12 months (and % of staff)
data_source: Phishing simulation platform
target_example: <= 2 % of staff, each with a targeted follow-up
pitfalls: Must be handled with care and never published by name; the metric is for targeting help, not blame. | Roles that receive many external emails (recruiting, finance) click more by exposure; compare within role.

name: Tier 1 vendors assessed within cadence
definition: Share of critical (Tier 1) vendors with a completed security assessment that is not older than the policy cadence (usually 12 months).
formula: Tier 1 vendors with a current assessment / Tier 1 vendors x 100
data_source: Vendor inventory and assessment register (see the vendor-risk-assessment-template repository)
pitfalls: Re-tiering vendors down to shrink the denominator; review tier changes. | A questionnaire returned is not an assessment completed; require the reviewer's rating.

name: Vendor assessments overdue
definition: Number of vendors (any tier) whose next-review date has passed without a completed re-assessment.
formula: count of vendors with next review date < today and no completed assessment since
data_source: Assessment register
pitfalls: Extending cadences in the policy to clear the backlog; document any cadence change. | Vendors with no assessment at all are not overdue in the formula; count them separately.

name: Critical vendor findings open beyond 90 days
definition: Findings rated High or Critical from vendor assessments that remain open more than 90 days after being agreed with the vendor.
formula: count of open High and Critical vendor findings older than 90 days
data_source: Assessment register, vendor remediation tracker
pitfalls: A finding the vendor disputes is still open; do not close on disagreement. | Compensating controls on your side can justify closure if they are documented.

name: Contracts with required security clauses
definition: Share of Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendor contracts that include all clauses marked Required for their tier (security obligations, incident notification, sub-processors, data return).
formula: contracts with all required clauses / Tier 1 and Tier 2 contracts x 100
data_source: Contract register, clause checklist
pitfalls: Legacy contracts cannot be changed until renewal; show the renewal date for the gaps. | A clause present but unenforceable (no audit right, no penalty) is cosmetic.

name: High-severity cloud misconfigurations open
definition: Number of open high-severity findings from cloud security posture scanning (public buckets, open security groups, missing logging, root keys in use).
formula: count of open findings rated High by the posture tool, after agreed exclusions
data_source: Cloud security posture management, native cloud security services
pitfalls: Exclusions become permanent; expire them automatically. | Severity scales differ between tools; normalise before comparing accounts.

name: Publicly accessible storage and databases
definition: Storage buckets, file shares and database instances reachable from the internet without authentication.
formula: count of storage and database resources with public access enabled
data_source: Cloud configuration export, posture management
target_example: 0 unapproved (approved public assets listed with an owner)
pitfalls: Web-hosting buckets are public on purpose; the approved list must distinguish them. | Databases exposed through a management port are missed if you only check storage.

name: Over-privileged cloud identities
definition: Cloud users, roles and service principals holding owner or administrator permissions that have not been used in 90 days, or permissions far wider than those used.
formula: count of identities with admin-level rights and no admin action in 90 days
data_source: Cloud IAM analytics, access analyser, activity logs
pitfalls: Break-glass accounts are unused by design; exclude them by name and review them separately. | Permissions inherited through groups are often missed by simple role listings.

name: Backup restore test success
definition: Share of critical systems for which a restore from backup was tested successfully, within the recovery-time objective, in the last quarter.
formula: critical systems with a successful restore test in the quarter / critical systems x 100
data_source: Backup platform reports, restore-test records
target_example: 100 % per year, >= 25 % per quarter on rotation
pitfalls: A successful backup job is not a successful restore; only restores count. | Immutable or offline copies should be a separate yes/no per system, or ransomware makes the metric meaningless.

name: AI systems inventoried
definition: Share of AI systems in use (built, bought or embedded in SaaS) that are recorded in the AI inventory with an owner, purpose and data used.
formula: AI systems in inventory with owner and purpose / AI systems discovered x 100
data_source: AI inventory reconciled with SaaS discovery, procurement and the vendor register
pitfalls: The denominator needs discovery (network, SaaS, browser extensions); the inventory cannot be its own reference. | AI features switched on inside existing SaaS tools are the usual blind spot.

name: AI systems with a completed impact assessment
definition: Share of AI systems rated medium or high impact that have a completed and approved AI impact assessment (risks to individuals, bias, data, misuse) before production use.
formula: AI systems with approved impact assessment / AI systems rated medium or high impact x 100
data_source: AI inventory, impact-assessment register
pitfalls: Assessments done after go-live still count but should be flagged; the point is before. | Rating everything 'low impact' empties the denominator; sample the low-impact list.

name: Unapproved AI applications in use
definition: Number of distinct AI applications or services observed in use (web proxy, SaaS discovery, browser extensions) that are not on the approved list.
formula: count of distinct AI services observed minus services on the approved list
data_source: Web proxy or secure web gateway, SaaS discovery, endpoint browser-extension inventory
target_example: Trend down; each new service triaged within 30 days
pitfalls: Blocking everything drives usage to personal devices; pair with an approved alternative. | Count services, not users, or one popular tool dominates the number.

name: AI incidents and model-monitoring alerts
definition: Confirmed incidents involving an AI system (data leakage through prompts, harmful output, prompt injection, model drift beyond threshold) in the period.
formula: count of AI-related incidents and triggered monitoring alerts per period
data_source: Incident register (AI tag), model monitoring, AI gateway logs
target_example: 0 confirmed data-leakage incidents; all alerts triaged
pitfalls: Without an AI tag in the incident process these incidents are filed as data leaks and never counted. | A monitoring threshold that never fires is probably set wrong, not a sign of a stable model.
